## Why

The post-merge verifier compares a PR against a diff that includes sibling PRs merged into the base branch between PR creation and merge. This misattributes files, can truncate the real subject files, and can cause incorrect closer-lane verdicts.

`.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js:614-621` uses `pull.base.sha` with `pull.merge_commit_sha`; `fetchLocalGitDiff` uses `git diff ${baseSha}...${headSha}`. Because the merge commit is on the base branch and `base.sha` is its ancestor, the range sweeps intervening base-branch history instead of only the PR diff. The fallback `fetchPullRequestDiff` is correct but runs only when the local diff is empty.

Observed in `stranske/learning-management-system` on 2026-09-10: #662 had no intervening merge and produced a correct report; #663 included #662's files; #665 included #663's files. Contamination also consumed `DEFAULT_DIFF_MAX_CHARS` (300000), truncating subject files. This affects every consumer of `stranske/Workflows/.github/workflows/reusable-agents-verifier.yml@main`.

## Scope

`.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js`, `templates/consumer-repo/.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js` (byte-identical and changed in lockstep), and `.github/scripts/__tests__/agents-verifier-context.test.js`.

## Non-Goals

Do not change the provider prompt, verdict schema, or `verifier_verdict_json.py`.

Do not raise diff character or byte budgets.

Do not retro-verify already-closed issues; LMS #656, #658, and the #663/#665 PR threads remain dispositioned.

A documentation-only comment without changing the range does not satisfy this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Replace the diff range in `.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js:614-621` so merged-PR context contains only that PR's diff.
- [ ] Update `templates/consumer-repo/.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js` with the identical change and keep it byte-identical to `.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js`.
- [ ] Add a test in `.github/scripts/__tests__/agents-verifier-context.test.js` stubbing `execFile`/`pulls.get` for a merged PR with one sibling commit after `base.sha`, asserting the diff includes the PR file and excludes the sibling file.
- [ ] Add a test in `.github/scripts/__tests__/agents-verifier-context.test.js` asserting `### File changes` lists exactly the PR's files.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For a merged PR with sibling commits between `base.sha` and `merge_commit_sha`, generated `## PR Diff (full)` and `### File changes` contain only the PR's files.
- [ ] Existing unmerged/push-path cases in `.github/scripts/__tests__/agents-verifier-context.test.js` pass unchanged.
- [ ] `npm test` or the repository JS test entry point passes for `.github/scripts/__tests__/`.
- [ ] Restoring `baseSha = pull.base?.sha` as the range left side makes the sibling-contamination test fail naming the sibling file; reverting makes it pass, with both transcripts recorded.
- [ ] A merged PR with an advanced base branch produces a provider-comparison report without an “unrelated changes” or “scope creep” caveat naming a file the PR does not touch.

## Implementation Notes

For merged PRs, use the merge commit’s first parent as the diff base: `${headSha}^` for squash merges or `git diff ${headSha}^1 ${headSha}` for merge commits. Do not use `pull.base.sha` as the left side when the right side is a base-branch merge commit.

Alternatively, prefer `fetchPullRequestDiff` for merged PRs and retain `fetchLocalGitDiff` only for unmerged/push paths. The REST diff is authoritative and the function already exists.

Explicitly guard the degenerate case where `merge-base(baseSha, headSha) === baseSha` and `headSha` is reachable from the base branch; document why the three-dot range is not the PR diff.

Do not raise `DEFAULT_DIFF_MAX_CHARS`; truncation is a symptom of contamination.

<details>
<summary>Original Issue</summary>

````text
<!-- workflow-source:local_request -->

## Why

The post-merge verifier grades a PR against a diff that also contains **every sibling PR merged into the base branch between that PR's creation and its own merge**. The verdict-bearing provider-comparison report therefore attributes other PRs' files to the PR under review, and — because the contaminated diff is larger — truncates the real subject files out of the context window. The closer lane closes source issues on these verdicts.

`.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js:614-621`:

```js
const baseSha = pull.base?.sha;
const headSha = pull.merge_commit_sha || pull.head?.sha || targetSha;
let diffText = fetchLocalGitDiff({ baseSha, headSha, ... });
```

`fetchLocalGitDiff` (line 218) runs `git diff --no-color ${baseSha}...${headSha}`. The three-dot form means `merge-base(baseSha, headSha)..headSha`. But `headSha` is `pull.merge_commit_sha`, a commit **on the base branch**, and `pull.base.sha` is an ancestor of it — GitHub records `base.sha` as the base-ref tip when the PR is opened and does not advance it as the branch moves. So `merge-base(base.sha, merge_commit) == base.sha`, the three-dot form degenerates to two-dot, and the range sweeps the whole stretch of base-branch history in between. The fallback immediately below (`fetchPullRequestDiff`, line 237, `pulls.get` with `mediaType: {format: 'diff'}`) returns the correct PR-only diff, but it runs only when the local diff comes back empty — and with `fetch-depth: 0` in `reusable-agents-verifier.yml:105` the local path succeeds, so the correct implementation is never reached.

## Observed instances (2026-09-10, stranske/learning-management-system)

Three consecutive verifier runs, with a natural control:

| PR | `base.sha` | `merge_commit_sha` | merged in between | report claimed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #662 | `89bad27009bc` | `0ebc108e1622` | *nothing* | correct — **no contamination caveat** |
| #663 | `89bad27009bc` | `ba28a8d418fd` | #662 (`0ebc108`) | *"also modifies `src/lms/maintenance/drafts.py` and adds `test_draft_approval.py`, `test_maintenance_loop_e2e.py` … this is scope creep"* — those are #662's files |
| #665 | `0ebc108e1622` | `c96e79170609` | #663 (`ba28a8d4`) | *"bundles unrelated changes to `src/lms/scheduling/repository.py` and associated scheduling test files (+90/-11, +73/-1)"* — those are #663's two test files, matching its line counts exactly |

#663's actual diff is three files (`src/lms/scheduling/repository.py` +19/-1 and two `tests/scheduling/` files); #665's is four files, none under `src/lms/scheduling/`. #662, with nothing merged in between, produced a clean report — which is what makes the mechanism, not coincidence, the explanation.

The harm compounds. Both reports also carried a caveat that the *real* subject file was truncated out of the context ("The full diff for `src/lms/scheduling/repository.py` … was truncated in the provided context, so the exact validation logic … could not be directly inspected"). That is the same cause: `formatDiffForContext` truncates at `DEFAULT_DIFF_MAX_CHARS` (300000, line 19), and the sibling commits consume the budget. So the verifier grades on files that are not the PR's while losing the files that are.

Both verdicts happened to be PASS, so nothing was mis-closed this time. The failure mode is not benign: an arm that sees a sibling's unrelated diff can lower confidence (both anthropic verdicts dropped to 68% and 72% on the contamination caveat), report scope creep that does not exist, or FAIL a PR for not implementing criteria while looking at another PR's files. The exposure is fleet-wide — every consumer repo calls `stranske/Workflows/.github/workflows/reusable-agents-verifier.yml@main`, and the rapid-merge cadence the lanes run at is exactly the condition that triggers it.

## Scope

`.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js` and its mirror `templates/consumer-repo/.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js` (currently byte-identical; both must change in lockstep), plus `.github/scripts/__tests__/agents-verifier-context.test.js`.

## Implementation Notes

1. The correct base for a merged PR's own diff is the merge commit's **first parent**: `${headSha}^` when `headSha` is `pull.merge_commit_sha`. For a squash merge that is exactly the PR's contribution; for a merge commit, `git diff ${headSha}^1 ${headSha}` is likewise the PR's contribution. Do not keep using `pull.base.sha` as the left side of a range whose right side is on the base branch.
2. Alternatively — and more simply — prefer `fetchPullRequestDiff` for the merged-PR case and keep `fetchLocalGitDiff` only for the unmerged/push path where no PR diff endpoint applies. The REST diff is authoritative for "what this PR changed" and the function already exists.
3. Whichever is chosen, guard the degenerate case explicitly: if `merge-base(baseSha, headSha) === baseSha` **and** `headSha` is reachable from the base branch, the three-dot range is not the PR's diff. A comment saying so is worth more than the fix, because the three-dot form looks correct on inspection.
4. Do not raise `DEFAULT_DIFF_MAX_CHARS` as the remedy. A larger budget hides the contamination instead of removing it, and the truncation caveat is a symptom.

## Tasks

- [ ] Replace the diff range in `agents_verifier_context.js:614-621` so a merged PR's context contains only that PR's diff.
- [ ] Mirror the identical change into `templates/consumer-repo/.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js` and confirm the two files stay byte-identical.
- [ ] Add a case to `.github/scripts/__tests__/agents-verifier-context.test.js` that stubs `execFile`/`pulls.get` for a merged PR whose base branch advanced by one sibling commit after `base.sha`, and asserts the produced diff contains the PR's own file and **not** the sibling's.
- [ ] Add a case asserting the emitted `### File changes` summary lists exactly the PR's files, since that summary is what the provider prompt leans on when the full diff is truncated.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For a merged PR with sibling commits between `base.sha` and `merge_commit_sha`, the generated context's `## PR Diff (full)` block and `### File changes` summary both list only the PR's own files.
- [ ] The unmerged/push path is unchanged: no regression in the existing `agents-verifier-context.test.js` cases.
- [ ] `npm test` (or the repo's JS test entry point) passes for `.github/scripts/__tests__/`.
- [ ] Deliberate-break: restore `baseSha = pull.base?.sha` as the range's left side and confirm the new sibling-contamination test fails naming the sibling's file; revert and confirm green. Quote both transcripts.
- [ ] Re-verification evidence: after the fix, one merged PR in a repo with an advanced base branch produces a provider-comparison report with no "unrelated changes"/"scope creep" caveat naming a file the PR does not touch.

## Non-Goals

- Do not change the provider prompt, the verdict schema, or `verifier_verdict_json.py`.
- Do not raise the diff character or byte budgets.
- Do not retro-verify already-closed issues; the three instances above are dispositioned in place (LMS #656, #658 and the #663/#665 PR threads).
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a comment documenting the three-dot degeneration without changing the range leaves every future report contaminated.
````
</details>

## Why

The weekly verifier-corpus harvest PR acquired a closing reference to design epic #2819 that it does not implement. On 2026-09-07, PR #3402 appended 126 lines to `config/model_eval_corpus_staging.json` but included `<!-- meta:issue:2819 -->` and `Closes #2819`, causing both verifier providers to grade it against #2819 and return FAIL.

This regressed between 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-07: six prior PRs on `verifier-corpus-harvest/auto` had neither a `meta:issue` marker nor a closing reference. The workflow at `.github/workflows/maint-79-verifier-corpus-harvest.yml:73` emits only `stranske/Workflows#2819`, which `.github/scripts/source_context.js:206-212` is written to reject. No binding-side code changed during the regression window.

A recurring harvest PR must not be verified against an unrelated implementation contract or close an open issue through the auto-merge path.

## Scope

_Not provided._

## Non-Goals

Do not reopen #2819; its disposition is recorded at https://github.com/stranske/Workflows/pull/3402#issuecomment-5572700622.

Do not change harvested content, `clean-pass` categorisation, or the auto-expiring staging split.

Do not suppress issue links globally; limit suppression to machine-authored recurring PRs.

Do not add scaffolding or TODO-only changes.

## Tasks

- [ ] Test how PR #3402 acquired `<!-- meta:issue:2819 -->` by inspecting the `Agents PR meta manager` run for `agents-pr-meta-v4.yml` on head `f294b789`, including whether `.github/scripts/agents_pr_meta_update_body.js:1119` wrote the marker, and record the finding in this issue.
- [ ] Update the existing dependency-promotion suppression mechanism in `.github/scripts/source_context.js:f2d406bf` so PRs opened by `maint-79-verifier-corpus-harvest.yml` cannot acquire closing issue references; cite the suppression file and line.
- [ ] Update `maint-79-verifier-corpus-harvest.yml:73` to emit an explicit non-closing provenance form that no extractor can read as a closing reference.
- [ ] Implement verifier handling that distinguishes recurring data-job PRs from issue implementations so harvest PRs are not graded against issue acceptance criteria.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/workflows/test_harvest_pr_source_binding.py::test_harvest_pr_body_yields_no_closing_reference` passes when the exact body from `maint-79-verifier-corpus-harvest.yml:73` is passed to `extractIssueNumbersFromText` at `.github/scripts/source_context.js:194`, asserting a result count of `0`.
- [ ] `tests/workflows/test_harvest_pr_source_binding.py::test_owner_repo_hash_reference_is_never_a_closing_reference` passes: `stranske/Workflows#2819` produces no closing reference, while a standalone `Closes #2819` does.
- [ ] Removing the `token.includes('/')` guard at `.github/scripts/source_context.js:208` causes `test_owner_repo_hash_reference_is_never_a_closing_reference` to fail; restoring the guard causes it to pass.

## Implementation Notes

Surfaced by the closer lane on 2026-09-07 while dispositioning PR #3402's verifier FAIL; verified against the merged diff, six prior harvest PR bodies, `source_context.js`, and binding-side commit history.

<details>
<summary>Original Issue</summary>

```text
## Why (verified evidence)

The weekly verifier-corpus harvest PR acquired a **closing reference to a design epic it does not implement**. On 2026-09-07, PR #3402 — a 126-line append to `config/model_eval_corpus_staging.json` and nothing else — opened with `<!-- meta:issue:2819 -->` and `Closes #2819` in its body. The verifier then graded it against #2819's five tasks and six acceptance criteria (workflow dispatch logic, promotion tiering, rollback metadata, three named test files) and returned **FAIL from both providers** (openai gpt-5.6-terra 95%, anthropic claude-sonnet-5 85%). Both verdicts are correct about the diff and wrong about the contract.

- **This is a regression, with a dated window.** The six prior harvest PRs on the identical branch `verifier-corpus-harvest/auto` carry no `meta:issue` marker and no closing reference: #3291 (2026-08-31), #3233 (2026-08-24), #3135 (2026-08-17), #3026 (2026-08-10), #2906 (2026-08-03), #2843 (2026-07-27). Only #3402 (2026-09-07) does. The change happened between 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-07.
- **The workflow body does not ask for it.** `.github/workflows/maint-79-verifier-corpus-harvest.yml:73` writes only `Automated corpus growth (stranske/Workflows#2819 move 2).` — a provenance mention in `owner/repo#N` form.
- **The extractor is written to reject exactly that form.** `.github/scripts/source_context.js:206-212`: the token preceding the `#` is tested with `token.includes('/')` and skipped, and `match.index > 0 && /\w/.test(value[match.index - 1])` skips it again because the character before `#` is `s` (from `Workflows`). So the documented path should not produce this binding.
- **No code change explains it.** `git`-side history shows the last change to `.github/scripts/source_context.js` was 2026-08-17 (`bc4cbe37`), to `.github/scripts/agents_pr_meta_update_body.js` 2026-06-19 (`9cee0b32`), to `.github/workflows/agents-pr-meta-v4.yml` 2026-08-24 (`e3212f0f`), and to `maint-79-verifier-corpus-harvest.yml` 2026-08-24 (`f1b4833d`). None falls inside the regression window. **The mechanism is not yet identified — finding it is task 1, not an assumption to be coded around.**
- **The damage this time was limited only by luck.** #2819 was closed on 2026-08-15, so merging #3402 misclosed nothing. Had it still been open, a scheduled JSON append would have closed a five-task design epic, and the auto-merge path in `maint-79-verifier-corpus-harvest.yml:83+` means no human would have been in the loop.

Consequence, recurring weekly: every harvest PR fails verification against a contract it never claimed, which trains the corpus-quality signal on a false negative and buries any real harvest defect in a standing FAIL. And any open issue this binding lands on gets closed by a data job.

## Tasks

- [ ] Identify how #3402 acquired `<!-- meta:issue:2819 -->` when the six prior PRs on the same branch did not, and when neither the workflow body nor any binding-side file changed in the window. Check the `Agents PR meta manager` run on #3402 (`agents-pr-meta-v4.yml`, `pull_request` event on head `f294b789`) and whether the marker was written by `agents_pr_meta_update_body.js:1119` or arrived some other way. Record the finding in this issue before editing anything.
- [ ] Once the path is known, stop it at the source for machine-authored recurring PRs: a PR opened by `maint-79-verifier-corpus-harvest.yml` must not acquire a closing reference to any issue. Cite the file:line where the suppression lands. `.github/scripts/source_context.js:f2d406bf` already established the precedent for dependency promotions ("suppress issue links for dependency promotions", #2862) — extend that mechanism rather than adding a parallel one.
- [ ] Make the recurring harvest PR carry an explicit non-closing provenance form in `maint-79-verifier-corpus-harvest.yml:73` that no extractor can read as a closing reference, so the correct behaviour does not depend on a guard elsewhere continuing to hold.
- [ ] Give the verifier a way to distinguish a recurring data job from an issue implementation, so a harvest PR is not graded against acceptance criteria at all. A FAIL that is structurally guaranteed is not a signal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Named test: `tests/workflows/test_harvest_pr_source_binding.py::test_harvest_pr_body_yields_no_closing_reference` — the exact body text produced by `maint-79-verifier-corpus-harvest.yml:73`, passed through `extractIssueNumbersFromText` (`.github/scripts/source_context.js:194`), yields an **empty** set. The test asserts on the count, not on truthiness, so a drained result of zero is a pass and not a failure.
- Named test: `tests/workflows/test_harvest_pr_source_binding.py::test_owner_repo_hash_reference_is_never_a_closing_reference` — `stranske/Workflows#2819` in a PR body produces no closing reference, and a bare `Closes #2819` on its own line still does.
- Deliberate-break → revert: remove the `token.includes('/')` guard at `.github/scripts/source_context.js:208` → confirm `test_owner_repo_hash_reference_is_never_a_closing_reference` FAILS → revert and confirm it passes.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT reopen #2819. It was closed on 2026-08-15 after #2831 and #2832 landed; the FAIL on #3402 was measured against the wrong contract and is not evidence that the epic is unfinished. The disposition is recorded at https://github.com/stranske/Workflows/pull/3402#issuecomment-5572700622.
- Do NOT change what the harvest job harvests, its `clean-pass` categorisation, or the auto-expiring staging split. The corpus content in #3402 is correct.
- Do NOT suppress issue links globally. Ordinary agent PRs must keep their closing references; the suppression is for machine-authored recurring PRs only.
- No scaffolding / TODO-only changes; every task is a concrete edit verified by the gate above.

_Surfaced by the closer lane on 2026-09-07 while dispositioning #3402's verifier FAIL; verified against the merged diff, the six prior harvest PR bodies, `source_context.js`, and the commit history of all four binding-side files._
```

## Why (verified evidence)

The belt dispatcher's queue-selection filters on the label `status:ready`, and **no code path in this repository ever applies that label.** Three paths remove it, none add it. Queue-selection can therefore never match, in any repo, and every belt claim in the last week came from a forced `workflow_dispatch` instead.

- **Selection predicate:** `.github/workflows/agents-71-codex-belt-dispatcher.yml:301` — `labels: \`agent:${agentKey},status:ready\`` on `issues.listForRepo`, an AND filter. The fallback message at `.github/workflows/agents-71-codex-belt-dispatcher.yml:316` confirms the intent: *"No open issues with labels `agent:<key>` and `status:ready` were found."*
- **Every write is a removal:** `.github/workflows/agents-71-codex-belt-dispatcher.yml:428` removes it on claim; `.github/workflows/agents-72-codex-belt-worker.yml` removes it again in its *"Remove residual status:ready label"* step; `scripts/cleanup_labels.py:159-161` lists both spellings for cleanup. `grep -rn 'status:ready' .github/ scripts/` returns reads and removals only — **there is no `addLabels` for `status:ready` anywhere.**
- **Live state, 2026-09-07:** across `Workflows`, `Inv-Man-Intake`, `Pension-Data` and `trip-planner`, the number of open issues carrying `status:ready` is **0**, and the number carrying the spaced variant `status: ready` is also **0**. The label population is empty in all four.
- **The label inventory has also drifted**, so even a manual application would miss in two repos: `Workflows` defines `status:in-progress` and `status: ready` (with a space); `Inv-Man-Intake` the same; `Pension-Data` defines only `status:in-progress` — no ready label of either spelling exists; `trip-planner` is the only repo defining the exact `status:ready` the code queries. `scripts/cleanup_labels.py:159-161` already carries both spellings, which is the tell that the drift was noticed and normalised for cleanup but never for the selection predicate.
- **Observed behaviour:** the last 12 `agents-71` runs in `Workflows` are all `workflow_dispatch`. There has been no dispatcher run at all since 2026-09-05T05:55:36Z.

Consequence: the belt has no working automatic queue. It advances only when someone forces a specific issue number, and the size of its real backlog is unobservable because the predicate that defines the queue selects an empty set by construction.

## Scope

- Define canonical ready label constant across `.github/workflows/agents-71-codex-belt-dispatcher.yml`, `.github/workflows/agents-72-codex-belt-worker.yml`, and `scripts/cleanup_labels.py`.
- Add the write side applying the ready label when an issue becomes eligible for the belt.
- Reconcile label definitions and update dispatcher empty queue reporting in `.github/workflows/agents-71-codex-belt-dispatcher.yml`.
- Add test coverage in `tests/workflows/test_belt_dispatcher_queue.py`.

## Implementation Notes

- Ensure `status:ready` constant is defined once and referenced uniformly across workflows and cleanup scripts.
- Ensure dispatcher distinguishes empty matching queue from unmatchable predicate configuration.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `.github/workflows/agents-71-codex-belt-dispatcher.yml`, `.github/workflows/agents-72-codex-belt-worker.yml`, and `scripts/cleanup_labels.py:159-161`, decide the single canonical spelling of the ready label and define it **once** as a named constant consumed by the dispatcher's selection filter, the dispatcher's removal, the worker's `hasReady` check, the worker's residual-removal step, and `scripts/cleanup_labels.py`.
- [ ] In `.github/workflows/agents-71-codex-belt-dispatcher.yml`, add the write side: whichever step marks an issue eligible for the belt must apply that constant.
- [ ] In `.github/workflows/maint-69-sync-labels.yml` and repository label configurations, reconcile the label definitions across the belt repos so the canonical name exists in each.
- [ ] In `.github/workflows/agents-71-codex-belt-dispatcher.yml:316`, make the dispatcher's "empty queue" report distinguish **"the predicate matched nothing"** from **"nothing in this repo can ever match the predicate"**.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Named test: `tests/workflows/test_belt_dispatcher_queue.py::test_ready_label_constant_is_shared` — the selection filter, both removal sites, the worker's `hasReady` check and `scripts/cleanup_labels.py` all resolve to the same label string, asserted by reading the single constant rather than by comparing two literals.
- Named test: `tests/workflows/test_belt_dispatcher_queue.py::test_ready_label_is_applied_somewhere` — at least one code path applies the ready label; the test fails if every occurrence in the tree is a read or a removal.
- Named test: `tests/workflows/test_belt_dispatcher_queue.py::test_empty_queue_distinguishes_no_match_from_no_possible_match` — with a repo whose label set cannot satisfy the predicate, the dispatcher emits the unsatisfiable-predicate message, not the ordinary empty-queue one, and that branch is reachable from a real input.
- Deliberate-break -> revert: change the dispatcher's selection filter back to a hardcoded `status:ready` literal while leaving the constant at its canonical value -> confirm `test_ready_label_constant_is_shared` FAILS -> revert and confirm it passes.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change the belt's forced-dispatch path (`.github/workflows/agents-71-codex-belt-dispatcher.yml:291-294`); manual dispatch by issue number stays exactly as it is.
- Do NOT widen the selection predicate to compensate — for example dropping the status requirement so every `agent:<key>` issue is selectable. The queue is meant to be opt-in; the defect is that nothing can opt in, not that the gate exists.
- Do NOT resolve this by mass-applying labels by hand; the fix is the missing write path plus the shared constant.
- No scaffolding / TODO-only changes; every task is a concrete edit verified by the gate above.

issues.body:
## Why (verified evidence)

The Codex belt's `status:in-progress` claim is a **write-only transition**: three code paths add it, and the single path that removes it cannot run unless a pull request already exists. An issue the belt claims but never works therefore stays claimed forever, and the state is silent — nothing reports it, so it reads as work in flight.

- **Added by** `.github/workflows/agents-71-codex-belt-dispatcher.yml:435` (dispatcher claim) and `.github/workflows/agents-72-codex-belt-worker.yml:1044` (worker claim).
- **Removed only by** `.github/workflows/agents-73-codex-belt-conveyor.yml:530`. That workflow is `workflow_call`-only and declares `pr_number` as `required: true` (`.github/workflows/agents-73-codex-belt-conveyor.yml:22-25`); its only caller is `.github/workflows/reusable-70-orchestrator-main.yml:3259`, which passes a concrete PR number. **Clearing the claim requires the very PR whose absence is the problem.**
- `docs/LABELS.md:730-733` states Agents 81 also clears the label after merging the linked PR. `grep -n 'status:in-progress' .github/workflows/` returns no drain step. The doc is wrong, and it is the only place a reader would look for the reclaim path.
- **Measured impact, 2026-09-07:** 13 open issues across 4 repos were latched, all claimed in a single dispatch burst by `agents-workflows-bot`, none with a linked PR, none with a commit, and no belt-dispatcher run in any of those repos since 2026-09-05T05:55:36Z. In Workflows the dispatcher had also created four `codex/issue-<n>` branches that were still at `ahead_by == 0` three days later.
- The closer lane released all 13 by hand on 2026-09-07 and deleted the four empty branches. **That is a manual drain, not a mechanism** — the next dispatch burst that fails to produce a PR relatches exactly the same way.

Consequence: every claimed-but-unworked issue is permanently invisible to both the belt (which selects on the absence of a claim) and to any lane that treats `status:in-progress` as a work lock, and the backlog it creates cannot be seen without querying GitHub by hand.

## Scope

- In `.github/workflows/health-40-sweep.yml`, add an automated reclaim step for stale `status:in-progress` issues without PRs.
- In `docs/LABELS.md`, update the label documentation to reflect the actual reclaim path.
- In `tests/workflows/test_belt_claim_reclaim.py`, provide automated test coverage for the reclaim logic.

## Implementation Notes

- Use a single shared constant for the claim timeout window in `.github/workflows/health-40-sweep.yml` and `.github/workflows/agents-71-codex-belt-dispatcher.yml`.
- Ensure sweep reports both latched and reclaimable counts clearly.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `.github/workflows/health-40-sweep.yml`, add a reclaim path that does not require a PR: for every open issue carrying `status:in-progress`, remove the label when there is no linked open or merged PR **and** the label has been present for longer than a single named constant.
- [ ] In `.github/workflows/health-40-sweep.yml` and `.github/workflows/agents-71-codex-belt-dispatcher.yml`, define that staleness window **once**, as a single constant consumed by both the claim side and the reclaim side, so the claiming window and the draining window cannot drift apart.
- [ ] In `.github/workflows/health-40-sweep.yml`, have the reclaim step post one comment on each reclaimed issue naming the claim timestamp and the absence of a PR, so the release is auditable rather than a silent label edit.
- [ ] In `.github/workflows/health-40-sweep.yml`, make the sweep report both quantities in the same place: the number of issues currently carrying `status:in-progress`, and the number of those that are reclaimable right now. The zero case must print a distinct, reachable 'none latched' line.
- [ ] Correct `docs/LABELS.md:730-733` to name the reclaim path that actually exists, and drop the Agents 81 claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Named test: `tests/workflows/test_belt_claim_reclaim.py::test_stale_claim_without_pr_is_reclaimed` — an open issue labelled `status:in-progress`, with no linked PR and a claim older than the constant, is reclaimed; an issue with a linked open PR is NOT reclaimed; an issue claimed inside the window is NOT reclaimed.
- Named test: `tests/workflows/test_belt_claim_reclaim.py::test_drained_state_reports_a_reachable_zero` — with no latched issues, the sweep prints its distinct 'none latched' output, and that branch is reached by an actual input rather than being unreachable dead text.
- Named test: `tests/workflows/test_belt_claim_reclaim.py::test_reclaimable_count_is_reported_alongside_blocking_count` — the sweep output carries both the in-progress count and the reclaimable count.
- Deliberate-break -> revert: change the reclaim condition to also require a linked PR (reintroducing the original latch) -> confirm `test_stale_claim_without_pr_is_reclaimed` FAILS -> revert and confirm it passes.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change what `status:in-progress` means, when the dispatcher or worker applies it, or the conveyor's PR-driven removal at `.github/workflows/agents-73-codex-belt-conveyor.yml:530`. That path is correct for the case it handles; this issue only adds the case it cannot handle.
- Do NOT have the sweep re-dispatch, re-label as ready, or otherwise restart work. It releases a false claim and reports; selection stays with the dispatcher.
- Do NOT add a second periodic workflow — extend the existing sweep.
- No scaffolding / TODO-only changes; every task is a concrete edit verified by the gate above.

issues.body:
## Why

`pr-00-gate.yml`'s **Report Gate commit status** step cannot write a commit status for a pull request opened from a fork: that event runs with a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/statuses/{sha}` answers `403 Resource not accessible by integration`. Every deployed Gate either rethrows that 403 or does not catch it at all, so the `summary` job fails **after** it has already computed a passing verdict — and the verdict is printed nowhere. A fork PR with entirely green CI reads as a red Gate, and the run looks like a broken check rather than a passing one.

Found live on `stranske/Fine-Art-Archive#716`, an outside contribution whose `lint-ruff`, `typecheck-mypy`, `python 3.12`, `python 3.13` and `logs summary` legs all passed: [run 34017696018, job `gate-summary`](https://github.com/stranske/Fine-Art-Archive/actions/runs/34017696018/job/101481301491).

This is a latched gate. Its clear path is blocked by the condition it measures — a fork PR can never write the status, so the Gate can never report — and nothing drains it. There is no external contribution path through CI in any repo on this list until it is fixed.

`.github/sync-manifest.yml` distributes `.github/workflows/pr-00-gate.yml` as `sync_mode: create_only` (`overwrite_repos: [stranske/Template]` only), so every consumer owns its own copy and **none of them will receive the upstream fix by sync**. Each needs its own PR.

## Scope

Port the guard already merged upstream to each affected consumer Gate, one bounded PR per repo.

Reference implementations:
- `stranske/Workflows#3398` — `.github/workflows/pr-00-gate.yml` and `templates/consumer-repo/.github/workflows/pr-00-gate.yml`, plus `tests/workflows/test_gate_commit_status_fork_tolerance.py`.
- `stranske/Fine-Art-Archive#717` — the same guard against the older deployed Gate shape, plus `tests/test_gate_commit_status_fork_tolerance.py`.

Remote scan on 2026-09-06 (each repo's `.github/workflows/pr-00-gate.yml` read from the GitHub contents API, not a local checkout):

| Repo | Shape | State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stranske/Fine-Art-Archive` | `hitRateLimit` | fix open (#717) |
| `stranske/Workflows` | `hitRateLimit` | fix open (#3398) |
| `stranske/Travel-Plan-Permission` | `hitRateLimit` | affected |
| `stranske/Counter_Risk` | `hitRateLimit` | affected |
| `stranske/Manager-Database` | `hitRateLimit` | affected |
| `stranske/Inv-Man-Intake` | `hitRateLimit` | affected |
| `stranske/Pension-Data` | `hitRateLimit` | affected |
| `stranske/Ready` | `hitRateLimit` | affected |
| `stranske/trip-planner` | `hitRateLimit` | affected |
| `stranske/learning-management-system` | `hitRateLimit` | affected |
| `stranske/Orchestrator` | `hitRateLimit` | affected |
| `stranske/Doc-Lineage` | `hitRateLimit` | affected |
| `stranske/Deliverable-Render` | `hitRateLimit` | affected |
| `stranske/Manager-Mosaic` | `hitRateLimit` | affected |
| `stranske/Template` | `hitRateLimit` | affected |
| `stranske/Collab-Admin` | `hitRateLimit` | affected |
| `stranske/Trend_Model_Project` | `isRateLimitError` (renamed variable, same defect) | affected |
| `stranske/Portable-Alpha-Extension-Model` | **no `try`/`catch` at all** — the 403 is unhandled | affected |

`stranske/Workflows-steward` has no `.github/workflows/pr-00-gate.yml` and is out of scope.

Two shapes need attention beyond a copy-paste: `Trend_Model_Project` names the predicate `isRateLimitError`, and `Portable-Alpha-Extension-Model` has no catch — it needs the whole `try`/`catch` added, not just the extra branch.

## Non-Goals

- Do not change `sync_mode` for `pr-00-gate.yml`. `create_only` is deliberate (consumers own their coverage/runtime policy); the point of this issue is that the sweep must be explicit.
- Do not touch `pull_request_target`, workflow `permissions`, token scope, or the token load balancer's `env: {}` pin.
- Do not widen the guard to any 403. A 403 on a **same-repo** PR is a genuine permission regression and must still fail the job — #2278 recorded the opposite defect, where a bare `status === 403` hid real permission failures behind rate-limit handling. Key the tolerance on the head repo differing from the base repo.
- Do not claim this makes branch protection satisfiable for fork PRs. With no status write there is still no `Gate / gate` status, so a protected branch still needs a maintainer. This only stops a *passing* fork Gate from reporting failure and makes the verdict readable.
- Do not batch all repos into one PR.

## Tasks

- [ ] For each affected repo, add the fork-token branch to the `Report Gate commit status` catch in `.github/workflows/pr-00-gate.yml`, keyed on `pull_request.head.repo.full_name !== pull_request.base.repo.full_name`, warning and writing the computed `state`/`description` to the log and `core.summary` instead of rethrowing.
- [ ] For `stranske/Portable-Alpha-Extension-Model`, add the missing `try`/`catch` around `createCommitStatus` before adding the branch.
- [ ] For `stranske/Trend_Model_Project`, apply the branch to the existing `isRateLimitError` predicate rather than renaming it.
- [ ] Port the test gate into each repo's suite (`tests/test_gate_commit_status_fork_tolerance.py`, or `tests/workflows/` where that layout exists), extracting the step's real script from the workflow file and executing it under Node.
- [ ] Record the deliberate-break result in each PR body: revert only `.github/workflows/pr-00-gate.yml` to its base content, show the named tests failing, restore exactly, show them passing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every repo in the table above (except the two with fixes already open) has a merged PR whose `.github/workflows/pr-00-gate.yml` tolerates a fork read-only 403 and rethrows a same-repo 403.
- [ ] Each such PR carries a test that executes the step's actual extracted script and asserts all four directions: fork 403 does not fail the job, same-repo 403 does, a non-403 does, and the rate-limit path is unchanged.
- [ ] Each PR body records the deliberate-break red output and the exact-restoration green output for its named test.
- [ ] A re-run of the remote scan reports `isForkPullRequest` present in every repo listed above.

## Implementation Notes

Re-run the scan before starting, and again at the end, rather than trusting local checkouts:

```bash
for r in Workflows Travel-Plan-Permission Trend_Model_Project Portable-Alpha-Extension-Model \
         Counter_Risk Manager-Database Inv-Man-Intake Pension-Data Ready trip-planner \
         learning-management-system Fine-Art-Archive Orchestrator Doc-Lineage \
         Deliverable-Render Manager-Mosaic Template Collab-Admin; do
  body=$(gh api "repos/stranske/$r/contents/.github/workflows/pr-00-gate.yml" --jq .content \
         | tr -d '\n' | base64 --decode)
  if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q isForkPullRequest; then s=FIXED
  elif printf '%s' "$body" | grep -qE 'hitRateLimit|isRateLimitError'; then s=AFFECTED
  else s=OTHER; fi
  echo "$r $s"
done
```

The number this issue is really about is not "18 repos" but "how many of them can report a verdict on a fork PR", which is currently zero. Say that number in the closing comment.

issues.body:
## Why

A codex-belt task can be recorded as `done` by the very commit that **starts** it, so the ledger reports work that was never performed. This is not a hypothetical: it happened on 2026-09-04 and the evidence is exact.

In `.agents/issue-3371-ledger.yml` on `main`, `task-01` reads:

```
    status: done
    started_at: '2026-09-04T20:08:35Z'
    finished_at: '2026-09-04T20:08:48Z'
    commit: 425953aa758c68e6d60d8432605514830cc1be02
```

Thirteen seconds elapsed between start and finish. Commit `425953aa` is titled **`chore(ledger): start task task-01 for issue #3371`** and its only changed file is `.agents/issue-3371-ledger.yml`. The artifact that task specifies, `docs/contracts/schemas/tracked-variable-v1.schema.json`, exists on neither `codex/issue-3371` nor `main`. The branch carries a single bootstrap commit.

Two independent tells confirm it rather than one:

- `task-02` in the same ledger asks for **the same file** and is still `todo`. A ledger that says a file was created and, three lines later, that it still needs creating, is reporting its own inconsistency.
- PR #3376, which merged that ledger, changed nothing else. An implementation-verification pass over 57 merged pull requests on 2026-09-05 flagged it and `stranske/trip-planner#1788` as the only two that delivered no implementation. Both are belt ledger merges.

**Why this is urgent rather than untidy.** The belt runs fleet-wide: 48 ledgers in this repository, 15 in trip-planner, 3 in Pension-Data at the time of writing. A task that can self-complete makes the ledger a source of false progress, and the ledger is what the keepalive and conveyor stages read to decide what remains. The owner is away until 2026-09-14, so nobody is watching the difference between "reported done" and "done".

## Scope

The belt's task-state transition: what may set `status: done`, and what evidence must exist before it may.

## Non-Goals

- No change to the belt's dispatch, branch naming or PR mechanics.
- No retroactive rewriting of existing ledgers in this issue. Correcting the historical record is a follow-up once the rule holds.
- Not a redesign of the belt. One transition is wrong; fix that.

## Tasks

- [ ] Find where the belt writes `status: done` (start from `.github/workflows/agents-72-codex-belt-worker.yml` and the belt scripts under `.github/scripts/`) and identify why the start-commit path can reach it.
- [ ] Require, before `done` may be written, that the cited commit changes **at least one file that is not the ledger itself**. A commit touching only `.agents/*-ledger.yml` may never complete a task.
- [ ] Reject `done` when the task names an artifact path that does not exist in the tree at that commit; record `status: blocked` with the reason instead, so the conveyor can see it.
- [ ] Make the ledger's own inconsistency fatal: if two tasks name the same artifact and one is `done` while the artifact is absent, fail the belt run rather than continuing.
- [ ] Emit the belt's counts together on every run: tasks `todo`, `in_progress`, `done`, `blocked`, including zeros, so a belt that completed nothing is distinguishable from a belt that never ran.
- [ ] Add a repair script that scans existing ledgers for `done` tasks whose commit touched only the ledger, and reports them without editing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A fixture ledger whose `done` commit touches only the ledger is rejected, and the error names the task id and the commit.
- [ ] A fixture task naming an absent artifact resolves to `blocked` with a reason, never `done`.
- [ ] A belt run that completes no tasks prints all four counts including zeros.
- [ ] The repair script, run against this repository, lists `issue-3371-ledger.yml` `task-01` and exits non-zero.
- [ ] A well-formed task whose commit adds a real file still reaches `done`, so the guard does not block legitimate progress.

## Test Gate

`tests/workflows/test_belt_ledger_completion.py`, run by the Gate. Demonstrate it by deliberately weakening the rule to allow a ledger-only commit to complete a task, confirming the rejection test fails, then reverting and confirming it passes. Record both outcomes in the pull request.

## Implementation Notes

This is a gate, so it owes the gate questions. What clears it: a commit that actually changes a non-ledger file, which the worker can produce while the gate is closed. What it measures and what drains it are the same set of tasks. What it prints when satisfied: the four counts above, including zeros, so a satisfied belt and a broken belt never look alike.

issues.body:
## Why

The identity-map conventions in `docs/contracts/identity-map-conventions.md` cover entities: managers, funds, consultants. They say nothing about **documents**, and the fleet's document-processing repos are about to need one shared answer. An inventory of the owner's work environment (2026-09-04) found that its document library has no stable document identifiers at all, that the filename is the de facto identifier, that supersession is an ad hoc numeric-prefix convention, and that one tool there already had to derive a content-hash identifier because a path-based key silently orphaned its data on rename. Four repos would otherwise each invent their own document identity: Doc-Lineage, Deliverable-Render, Inv-Man-Intake and Pension-Data.

Evidence: response sections C9 and C10 (https://github.com/stranske/Ready/blob/main/research-program/artifacts/work-bundle/INFORMATION-REQUEST-RESPONSE.md); `docs/contracts/identity-map-conventions.md` entity-only vocabulary; `docs/contracts/evidence-object-v1.md` and its schema, which carry an entity reference but no document identity field.

## Scope

Extend the contract set with a document-identity convention and a document reference shape that evidence objects can carry, owned here and adopted by the document-processing repos.

## Non-Goals

No central resolver service and no shared Python package. This is a convention plus a schema, consistent with how the identity-map conventions are already owned.
No change to the entity identity vocabulary.
No requirement that any repo adopt it in this issue; adoption lands in the consuming repos.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `docs/contracts/document-identity-conventions.md` defining a document identity as content-first: `sha256` of the bytes as the primary key, with a human-readable `doc_key` of `{entity_ref}/{doc_type}/{as_of}` as a secondary index that is explicitly not unique.
- [ ] Define a closed `doc_type` vocabulary covering the categories the fleet actually processes: call note, manager letter, data packet, legal document, consultant report, research article, marketing material, regulatory filing, audited financial statement, questionnaire, internal diligence report, presentation.
- [ ] Define the supersession fields `supersedes` and `supersession_evidence`, requiring that the evidence name the mechanism that established the relationship rather than asserting it bare.
- [ ] Define `text_basis` as `native | ocr | mixed | unknown` and require that any coverage or completeness figure derived from document text carry it, so a figure computed without recognition is legible as a floor.
- [ ] Add a `document_ref` block to `evidence-object/v1`: `sha256, doc_key, doc_type, page, text_basis`, with `page` required when the evidence quotes text.
- [ ] Update `schemas/evidence-object-v1.schema.json` accordingly and add fixtures for a native-text and a recognized-text evidence object.
- [ ] Extend `scripts/validate_run_contract.py` to validate the new block and reject an evidence object that quotes text without a page.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The validator rejects an evidence object with a quote and no page, and one with a `doc_type` outside the vocabulary.
- [ ] The validator rejects a coverage figure carrying `text_basis` absent, rather than defaulting it to `native`.
- [ ] Existing fixtures that carry no `document_ref` still validate, so the change is additive for current participants.
- [ ] Both new fixtures validate and are exercised by the existing contract-integrity workflow.
- [ ] ## Test Gate
- [ ] The repository's existing contract tests plus a new `tests/contracts/test_document_identity.py`, run by the Gate. Demonstrate it by deliberately defaulting `text_basis` to `native` when absent, confirming the rejection test fails, then reverting and confirming it passes. Record both in the pull request.

## Implementation Notes

Keep the convention document parallel in structure to `identity-map-conventions.md`, including its "convention, not central code" framing: resolution stays in the repos that own their corpora. The load-bearing rule is content-first identity, because the target environment renames files routinely and a path-keyed store silently loses data when it happens.

## Summary

The consumer template's `generated-delivery-wakeup` job fires a cross-repo
`repository_dispatch` into `stranske/Workflows` using `WRITE_TOKEN`. That token is not
authorized for the target repo, so the step throws a non-retryable `HttpError` and the whole
`Agents Gate Followups` run is marked `failure` — in every consumer repo, on every Gate
completion for a `sync/workflows-*` or `deps/sync-dev-versions-*` branch.

Observed today (2026-09-04), same failing job and step in three repos:

| Repo | Run | Job | Failing step |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stranske/Travel-Plan-Permission` | [33884908164](https://github.com/stranske/Travel-Plan-Permission/actions/runs/33884908164) | `Wake generated delivery reconciler` | `Dispatch exact generated lane to Workflows` |
| `stranske/Portable-Alpha-Extension-Model` | [33884930515](https://github.com/stranske/Portable-Alpha-Extension-Model/actions/runs/33884930515) (also 33868050096) | same | same |
| `stranske/learning-management-system` | [33872494459](https://github.com/stranske/learning-management-system/actions/runs/33872494459) | same | same |

Annotation on the TPP run:

```
Unhandled error: HttpError: Resource not accessible by personal access token
 - https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/repos#create-a-repository-dispatch-event
```

`Resource not accessible by **personal access token**` (not `by integration`) means the fallback
chain at `templates/consumer-repo/.github/workflows/agents-81-gate-followups.yml:56-60`
(`AGENTS_AUTOMATION_PAT || ACTIONS_BOT_PAT || SERVICE_BOT_PAT || github.token`) resolved a PAT
whose resource scope does not include `stranske/Workflows`.

## What is NOT broken (checked, so this is not filed as a starvation)

`Merge Sync PRs` (`maint-71-merge-sync-prs.yml`) is running fine — 12 successful runs in
`stranske/Workflows` today between 10:59Z and 14:55Z, all via `workflow_dispatch`, none via
`repository_dispatch`. The reconciler is being woken by another route, so sync PRs are **not**
starved. This dispatch path is a redundant wakeup that is dead, and its only current effect is
noise.

That noise is the actual cost: `Agents Gate Followups` goes red in consumer repos for a reason
that has nothing to do with the PR under test, which is exactly the condition that trains readers
(and closer lanes) to discount a red Gate Followups run. This surfaced while auditing why
Fine-Art-Archive #680 looked unhealthy.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `templates/consumer-repo/.github/workflows/agents-81-gate-followups.yml`, stop letting a
  cross-repo authorization failure fail the run. The wakeup is best-effort and provably redundant:
  catch the non-retryable authorization error (403/404 from `createDispatchEvent`), emit
  `core.notice`/`core.warning` naming the token that was tried and the target, and exit the step
  successfully. Keep the existing `withRetry` behaviour for 429/5xx.
- [ ] Do not broaden the failure swallow: a 5xx after retries, or any other status, must still fail
  so a genuinely broken dispatch is still visible.
- [ ] Mirror the change into any other cross-repo `createDispatchEvent` call in the same template
  that has the same best-effort character (audit `env.WRITE_TOKEN` uses at lines 1381, 1442, 1812,
  1889, 2090, 2164 and change only the ones that are genuinely best-effort).
- [ ] Add a test in `tests/workflows/` asserting the step yaml handles the authorization error
  branch, so the swallow cannot silently widen later.

## Test gate

Named gate: the new `tests/workflows/` case for the `generated-delivery-wakeup` error handling,
plus the existing consumer-template parity tests.

Deliberate-break demonstration required in the PR: with the fix in place, revert only the
error-handling branch (let the 403 propagate) and show the new test going RED, then restore it and
show it GREEN. Paste both blocks.

## Non-goals

- Do not rotate, mint, or re-scope any PAT in this issue, and do not add a new secret name to the
  fallback chain. If the owner later widens `AGENTS_AUTOMATION_PAT` to include `stranske/Workflows`,
  the dispatch starts working again and this change stays correct either way.
- Do not remove the `generated-delivery-wakeup` job. It is the intended fast path; only its failure
  mode is wrong.
- Do not touch `maint-71-merge-sync-prs.yml` or the sync-PR lifecycle.
- No scaffolding: no new workflow, no new script, no config toggle.
